text:
[LCCO.5.2] To make capture work across the outer rule's
firing-time and the continuation's matching-time, the compiler
must emit a synthetic capture fact alongside the lowered `call`:

```
$CaptureBindings_<outer>_c<N>
  corr <corr>
  <field>: <snapshot value> ...
```

The capture fact carries snapshot values of each LHS binding the
continuation bodies reference. Each `on` and `error` sibling must include this
fact in its LHS, joined on `corr`. A `timeout` sibling joins its timer instead,
which carries the correlation and the values its body reads ([LCCO.7.2]).

**The fact is emitted for every call with continuations, even with nothing to
capture.** A generated correlation is per activation ([LCCO.3.4]), and
so is an `as` whose value is computed from the firing — a binding, a slot read or
an interpolated string — so this fact is what carries the correlation from the
firing to the `on` and `error` siblings; a call whose continuation bodies reference no binding
emits it with the `corr` slot alone. Only a call whose `as` is a compile-time
constant, a plain literal or a `const`, may omit it when there is nothing to
capture, because the siblings then match that constant directly.
